## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (the two `record()` call sites around the structured and agentic run paths, plus the `_call_label` fallback at runner.py:590) reads `req.target.get(\"ticket_id\")` when building the usage-log row, but every producer of `target` writes the plural key `ticket_ids` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` and `src/rebar/llm/operations.py`). Result: 0 of the ~11,900 rows in `.rebar/usage.jsonl` carry a ticket, so per-ticket (and therefore per-review) cost attribution from the usage log is impossible, and `docs/llm-framework.md`'s claim that rows carry `ticket` is false. The eval ledger needs per-run attribution and this is the cheapest fix on that path.

## Approach

At all three read sites (the two `record()` call sites and the `_call_label` fallback at runner.py:590), read `ticket = target.get(\"ticket_ids\")` and take `ticket = ticket_ids[0] if ticket_ids else None` — producers always write `ticket_ids` as a list (possibly empty), never omit the key, so the empty-list case is the real path to handle, not a missing key. Drop the backward-compat read of the singular `ticket_id` key: no producer writes it, so it is a dead shim with no live consumer. Correct the doc sentence in `docs/llm-framework.md`. If a run's `ticket_ids` has more than one element (a multi-ticket/graph run), only the first is attributed to the usage row — this is a known simplification, not full multi-ticket attribution; that is out of scope here.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (three read sites: both `record()` call sites and `_call_label`)
- `docs/llm-framework.md`
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` (or the existing runner usage test)

## Testing

Unit: a request whose target carries `ticket_ids=[id]` yields a usage row with `ticket == id`; a request whose target carries `ticket_ids=[id_a, id_b]` yields `ticket == id_a` (first-element rule, pinned by test); a request whose target carries `ticket_ids=[]` (the real empty-list producer path) yields `ticket=None`; a request whose target omits `ticket_ids` entirely also yields `ticket=None`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New usage-log rows produced by a gate session carry the ticket id; checked by running one `review-plan` locally (or the Tier-1 commissioning run) and inspecting the rows.
- [ ] The regression tests above (single element, multi-element first-wins, empty list, missing key) pass in `make test`.
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` describes the actual field and the first-element attribution rule for multi-ticket runs.
